examples.title: Induction motor: AC equivalent-circuit identification
examples.summary: Identify a linear squirrel-cage induction motor circuit from stationary AC frequency-sweep phase-linkage results, then use the circuit to infer operating behavior.
assumptions: The source example is a 4-pole, 36-stator-slot and 28-rotor-slot machine.
The reference quarter model uses paired anti-periodic edges.
Rotor currents are induced in conductive bars; stator iron eddy currents are neglected.
Phase quantities and RMS/peak conventions are explicit; the example uses a delta connection.
limitations: The linear identification does not cover closed rotor-slot bridges requiring saturation.
End rings, axial leakage, rotor temperature, skew and additional losses require separate corrections.
A static mesh is used; this is not a direct time-domain motion simulation.

examples.title: Induction motor: imposed-current magnetostatic iteration
examples.summary: Analyze on-load induction-motor conditions with magnetostatic solutions coupled to a rotor-field-oriented analytical model and an equivalent rotor winding.
assumptions: Stator and rotor currents are explicitly imposed rather than induced by an AC conductor solve.
The equivalent rotor winding follows source slot-angle and winding-factor relations.
The source relies on a dq/RFO description and its stated spatial-field assumptions.
limitations: An arbitrary rotor-current snapshot is not this complete procedure.
Rotor impedance, field orientation and iterative convergence must be supplied.
Current-angle and winding normalization conventions cannot be borrowed blindly from synchronous-machine examples.

examples.title: LRK BLDC: phase-linkage and cogging-torque sweep
examples.summary: Sweep the LRK motor rotor through angle with zero coil currents to record magnet-produced phase linkages and cogging torque.
assumptions: The supplied flux_femm42.lua is a FEMM 4.2 reference script.
The script zeros phases A, B and C and rotates the source rotor group.
Cogging torque refers to the unenergized-winding state.
limitations: The original script and material names need a FEMM 5 compatibility check.
The original fixed geometry does not by itself supply a generalized tooth-construction algorithm.
Group number 2 is source-specific and must not be assumed for other models.

examples.title: BLDC motion with a periodic air-gap boundary
examples.summary: Represent rotor displacement with a periodic or anti-periodic air-gap boundary while retaining the bulk rotor/stator meshes, then obtain smooth linkage, voltage and cogging traces.
assumptions: The documented motion capability appears in FEMM builds from 25 February 2018.
The example uses a symmetry-consistent air-gap boundary and a source-defined BLDC geometry.
Some benchmark dimensions and materials were inferred or selected rather than fully specified by the original reference paper.
limitations: A stationary mesh alone does not demonstrate numerical convergence.
Boundary sign and inner/outer angle depend on modeled sector and which body moves.
Source waveform agreement is not an independent local verification by this graph.

examples.title: Air-gap motion: dipole torque benchmark
examples.summary: Benchmark air-gap-boundary rotor motion against the analytic torque of a unit-permeability magnet in a uniform external magnetic field.
assumptions: The bar magnet is 1 cm by 0.5 cm with a 2 cm planar depth.
The source uses relative permeability 1, coercivity 1 MA/m and an external field of 1 T.
The source angle definition yields a 1 N*m sine torque curve.
limitations: The uniform-field construction and unit-permeability moment assumptions are essential.
Published numerical agreement remains a source-reported benchmark until rerun.

examples.title: SPM motor: core, magnet and proximity-loss histories
examples.summary: Collect angle-dependent field histories in a concentrated-winding SPM machine and estimate core, magnet and winding proximity losses through separate postprocessing models.
assumptions: The source machine has 16 magnets and 18 stator slots.
Magnetostatic field solutions neglect the direct reaction of the modeled loss mechanisms under the stated approximation.
The example assumes laminated stator and rotor cores and source-specific material/loss data.
limitations: Loss coefficients and their fitted frequency ranges are material-specific.
Magnet reaction fields and high-frequency proximity behavior can invalidate the selected approximations.
Axial/end-turn and thermal corrections remain separate from the 2D field solve.

examples.title: Outrunner DSPM generator: load point and core loss
examples.summary: Combine a circuit approximation and rotating field histories to estimate core losses under load in an outer-rotor doubly salient permanent-magnet generator.
assumptions: The illustrative generator target is 500 W at 5000 rpm and 48 V peak.
Both rotor and stator cores are laminated but see different material-frame frequency content.
The example assumes stated winding and magnet temperatures instead of solving a coupled thermal problem.
limitations: Incremental inductance cannot be found from total PM-biased linkage divided by current.
The source core-loss study omits some additional loss mechanisms and does not establish full machine efficiency.
The unusual example topology is not a universal generator design.

examples.title: Outrunner BLDC: constrained random geometry optimization
examples.summary: Search a parameterized 14-magnet outrunner design for reduced size at a specified winding current density and torque requirement.
assumptions: Each accepted candidate is evaluated by finite-element analysis.
The objective uses torque per unit axial length to infer the length required by the target.
A shrinking random-search neighborhood is used after a stall criterion.
limitations: Best observed fitness is not a proof of global optimality.
Mesh-related objective discontinuities must be tolerated and checked.
Geometry, current-density and torque constraints must remain fixed during comparisons.

examples.title: Inset PM motor: frozen-permeability field separation
examples.summary: Reproduce a loaded nonlinear PM operating point and source-separated frozen-permeability solutions to inspect current and permanent-magnet field contributions.
assumptions: The source reference is an 18-slot, 6-pole inset-PM machine.
The whole-field state uses both PMs and the specified phase currents.
Several source geometry/material choices were inferred or assumed and must retain that provenance.
limitations: Source-separated frozen fields are tied to the loaded permeability state.
This page does not by itself establish a general average-torque separation workflow.
FEMM builds must support the relevant previous-solution/frozen-permeability capability.

examples.title: Eight-pole radial bearing: nonlinear force and bias
examples.summary: Check force and magnetic-circuit approximations for an eight-pole radial bearing, including a bias-current small-signal interpretation.
assumptions: Four opposed horseshoe-like actuators surround the rotor.
Adjacent coils use the documented reverse-series polarity.
Simple force linearization is about the stated centered bias condition.
limitations: Leakage, fringing and nonlinear iron reluctance change the ideal circuit estimates.
A static magnetic model does not establish active-control stability or rotor dynamics.

examples.title: Radial bearing: rotational electromagnetic loss and windage
examples.summary: Iterate vector-potential harmonic rotor-surface boundary conditions to estimate rotational electromagnetic losses, and evaluate windage separately.
assumptions: The source Octave script parameterizes an eight-pole bearing.
A harmonic rotor-loss model is converted to element-level boundary data through spatial transforms.
Air properties and cylinder-clearance correlations determine the separate windage calculation.
limitations: A scalar local impedance cannot replace the coupled spatial-harmonic procedure.
The electromagnetic and mechanical loss estimates have different assumptions and evidence.
The source benchmark values are not new local numerical results.

examples.title: Magnetization patterns: diametral, radial and Halbach

assumptions: Magnetization patterns must represent actual manufacture or a clearly stated idealization.
Position expressions use the model coordinate system and consistent lengths.
limitations: A continuous field pattern differs from a segmented physical array.
Exact source geometry and material properties remain required for numerical reproduction.

examples.title: Modified Halbach arrays: repeated double magnet layer
examples.summary: Inspect the inter-magnet field of an infinite repeated double-layer modified Halbach array using parameterized Octave construction scripts.
assumptions: A repeated infinite-array idealization is used.
Zero interMagnet selects the source true-Halbach configuration.
Backing plates provide mechanical binding; the source model uses steel plates in its illustrated modified configuration.
limitations: A finite physical array can have end effects absent from the idealization.
The source does not establish a motor torque or complete electrical operating-point model.

examples.title: Coreless three-phase alternator with dual magnet layers

assumptions: The source reference has four pole pairs, six bobbins and a 40 mm planar magnet length.

The source winding outline uses curved-end trapezoids rather than exact manufactured coil geometry.
The source script uses a translated construction center; coordinate-dependent operations must use that actual center.
limitations: The source script is parameterized but explicitly not foolproof for arbitrary designs.
Its old coil-inductance extraction was found not meaningful; distributed capacitance can matter for very low inductance.
